Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m starting with `README.md`, then I’ll apply the required wake-visual-signal skill before touching the target policy. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and won’t consult the omitted research shelf or neighboring runs.

The wake-visual skill requires the qualitative diagnosis to be anchored to observations, metrics, diagnostics, and both prewarm/rollout keyframes before any policy edit. I’m now collecting those sources and the inherited guidance/log history; the candidate file will remain untouched until the required notes are written.

The current split-guard rollout is a mixed result: it has the best scalar score and slightly lower mean distance, but it arrives 2.22 units later, loses upstream-relative speed, raises energy, and increases force/moment despite lower tail authority. The visuals agree—the final correction is deeper—so the original “tail clipping reduces load” hypothesis does not survive. I’m checking the policy-state contract now to select one bounded follow-on mechanism rather than treating the scalar gain as a clean win.

The skill’s visual comparison now has a concrete control implication: posterior limit 27 creates more phase-distorting saturation, not less load. I’ll record that diagnosis before editing, then make a single follow-on probe: restore the proven 28 tail guard and raise only posterior velocity damping from 0.65 to 0.67. This keeps the successful bearing/gait package fixed while testing smoother transient suppression upstream of the guard.

The candidate, provenance notes, and durable guidance are now all updated. The reusable lesson records the split guard as a scalar/route tradeoff but a negative load-control result, and it also removes the stale recommendation to interpolate steering gain below 0.75 after the evaluated 0.745 regression. I’m moving through the mandated configured checks now.

The mandated guidance check found a duplicated “copied to guidance” parent marker in the rendered workspace `README.md`, so it could not identify the assigned parent. I’m removing only the duplicate marker, as required to make the configured parent comparison well-defined, then I’ll rerun the check.

Two configured checks pass: semantic guidance and editable boundary. The Julia contract command cannot run because `julia` is absent from this environment (exit 127), so I’m completing the available deterministic/static contract checks and reviewing the final diff; no CFD will be run.

I’ve run the configured commands directly; to satisfy the workspace’s explicit “invoke check-runner” requirement literally, I’m also handing the final tree to the configured read-only check runner for an independent PASS/FAIL report. It will not edit files or run CFD.
